title: Cancellation along a proper surjection
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $h:Y\to Z$ be proper morphisms of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], with $f$ surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] (the composite $hf:X\to Z$ is then proper). If $\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ and $\mathrm{PBC}(hf)$ hold in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-property], then $\mathrm{PBC}(h)$ holds.

proof.text: *Reduction to injective acyclicity.* The composite $hf$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. By [lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity] applied to the proper morphisms $f$ and $hf$, the hypotheses $\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ and $\mathrm{PBC}(hf)$ give $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ and $\mathrm{IA}_r(hf)$ for every prime $r$ [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property]; by the same lemma applied to the proper morphism $h$, it suffices to prove $\mathrm{IA}_r(h)$ for every prime $r$. Fix a prime $r$, a morphism of schemes $c:Z'\to Z$ and an injective object $I$ of the category of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$; we must show $R^ph'_*b^{-1}I=0$ for $p>0$, where $b:Y'\to Y$, $h':Y'\to Z'$ are the maps of a cartesian square completing $h$ and $c$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first sentences ("We will use the equivalence of Lemma 0A4B without further mention. Let $\ell$ be a prime number. Let $\mathcal I$ be an injective sheaf of $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$-modules on $Y_{\acute etale}$"); Lemma 0A4B (label lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives)

proof.text: *$I$ is a direct summand of $f_*J$.* The inverse image $f^{-1}I$ is a sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] (with $T=X$, $R=\mathbf F_r$) choose a monomorphism $f^{-1}I\hookrightarrow J$ with $J$ injective in the category of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$. Since $f$ is surjective, [lem-weil-pbc-retract-supplied] (read in the categories of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules, where its argument takes place) shows that the adjoint map $\iota:I\to f_*J$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is a monomorphism and, $I$ being injective, that there is a retraction $\rho:f_*J\to I$ with $\rho\iota=\mathrm{id}_I$. So it suffices to prove the desired vanishing for $f_*J$ (step 6).

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Choose an injective map of sheaves $f^{-1}\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ ... Since $f$ is surjective the map $\mathcal I\to f_*\mathcal J$ is injective (look at stalks in geometric points). Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$. Thus it suffices to prove the desired vanishing for $f_*\mathcal J$.")

proof.text: *The base-changed diagram.* Let $X'$ with $a:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ complete $f$ and $b$ to a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], $X'\cong X\times_YY'$. The lower square ($Y'\to Y$ over $Z'\to Z$) is cartesian, so by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the outer rectangle, with vertical maps $hf$ and $h'f'$ and horizontal maps $a$ and $c$, is cartesian: $X'\cong X\times_ZZ'$, and $h'f':X'\to Z'$ is the base change of $hf$ along $c$ with projection $a$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, second paragraph ("set $Y'=Z'\times_ZY$ and $X'=Z'\times_ZX=Y'\times_YX$. Denote $a:X'\to X$, $b:Y'\to Y$ ... $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':Y'\to Z'$")

proof.text: *Underived exchange.* $J$ is killed by $r$, hence a torsion sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Since $f$ is proper, [lemma-weil-pbc-proper-underived-exchange] applied to the cartesian square of step 3 ($f$, $f'$, $b$, $a$) and to $J$ gives an isomorphism $b^{-1}f_*J\cong f'_*a^{-1}J$ of sheaves on $Y'_{\Et}$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, second paragraph ("By Lemma 0A3U we have $b^{-1}f_*\mathcal J=f'_*a^{-1}\mathcal J$"); Lemma 0A3U (label lemma-proper-base-change-f-star)

proof.text: *The two vanishings.* $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$, applied to the base change $b:Y'\to Y$ of step 3 and the injective $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaf $J$, gives $R^qf'_*a^{-1}J=0$ for $q>0$. $\mathrm{IA}_r(hf)$, applied to the base change $c:Z'\to Z$ with the cartesian outer rectangle of step 3 and to $J$, gives $R^n(h'f')_*a^{-1}J=0$ for $n>0$. Both are instances of [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property], with $R^q$ the higher direct images of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, second paragraph ("On the other hand, we know that $R^qf'_*a^{-1}\mathcal J$ and $R^q(g'\circ f')_*a^{-1}\mathcal J$ are zero for $q>0$")

proof.text: *Spectral sequence.* [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence] for $X'\xrightarrow{f'}Y'\xrightarrow{h'}Z'$ and $F=a^{-1}J$ gives a first-quadrant spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=R^ph'_*R^qf'_*a^{-1}J\Rightarrow R^{p+q}(h'f')_*a^{-1}J$. By step 5, $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $q>0$ and the abutment vanishes in every degree $n>0$, so [lem-weil-pbc-first-quadrant-row-collapse] gives $R^ph'_*(f'_*a^{-1}J)=E_2^{p,0}=0$ for $p>0$. Since $R^ph'_*$ is a functor, the isomorphism of step 4 gives $R^ph'_*(b^{-1}f_*J)=0$ for $p>0$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, second paragraph ("Using the spectral sequence (Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 0734) $R^pg'_*R^qf'_*a^{-1}\mathcal J\Rightarrow R^{p+q}(g'\circ f')_*a^{-1}\mathcal J$ we conclude that $R^pg'_*(b^{-1}f_*\mathcal J)=R^pg'_*(f'_*a^{-1}\mathcal J)=0$ for $p>0$ as desired")

proof.text: *Descent to the summand and conclusion.* The functor $b^{-1}$ is additive [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], so $b^{-1}\rho\circ b^{-1}\iota=\mathrm{id}_{b^{-1}I}$: $b^{-1}I$ is a direct summand of $M=b^{-1}f_*J$. By step 6 $R^ph'_*M=0$ for $p>0$, so [lem-weil-pbc-vanishing-descends-retract] (for $h'$, $M$ and its summand $b^{-1}I$) gives $R^ph'_*b^{-1}I=0$ for $p>0$. As $c$ and $I$ were arbitrary, $\mathrm{IA}_r(h)$ holds [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property]; as $r$ was arbitrary, step 1 ([lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity] for the proper $h$) gives $\mathrm{PBC}(h)$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("$\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$. Thus it suffices to prove the desired vanishing for $f_*\mathcal J$") and the opening sentence (equivalence of Lemma 0A4B)

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper and surjective and $h:Y\to Z$ proper. If $f$ and
$hf$ satisfy $\mathsf{IA}$, then $h$ satisfies $\mathsf{IA}$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Fix a base change $a:Z'\to Z$ and an injective $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf
$I$ on $Y$. Choose a
monomorphism $f^{-1}I\hookrightarrow J$ with $J$ injective on $X$. Applying
$f_*$ gives $\iota:I\to f_*J$. If a germ $a\in I_{\bar y}$ maps to zero,
choose a geometric $\bar x\to X$ above $\bar y$ (surjectivity). The canonical
stalk identification $(f^{-1}I)_{\bar x}\cong I_{\bar y}$ sends $a$ to the
germ of $a$ at $\bar x$; the monomorphism into $J$ makes that germ zero. The
definition of the direct-image stalk then says that $a$ vanishes on an etale
neighbourhood of $\bar y$, so $a=0$. Thus $\iota$ is monic. Injectivity of $I$ supplies a retraction
$r:f_*J\to I$ with $r\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_I$, making $I$ a direct summand.
After base change, proper underived exchange gives
$b^{-1}f_*J\cong f'_*a_X^{-1}J$. The spectral sequence

$$
R^ph'_*R^qf'_*a_Y^{-1}I\Longrightarrow R^{p+q}(h'f')_*a_X^{-1}I
$$

is computed using the injective $J$ and the assumed acyclicity of $hf$.
The $q>0$ terms vanish for $J$ by $\mathsf{IA}(f)$, and total-degree
vanishing for $hf$ forces $R^ph'_*a_Y^{-1}(f_*J)=0$ for $p>0$. Derived
direct image preserves finite direct sums and retracts, so the same vanishing
holds for the direct summand $a_Y^{-1}I$. This is Tag `0A4C`; the
stalk injectivity argument is written here because surjectivity is essential.

split_report.summary: Rewrote the proof from Stacks Lemma 0A4C (lemma-sandwich), the cancellation lemma used in the proof of 0A4F, in seven steps each citing the place. Statement: f, h proper, f surjective, PBC(f), PBC(hf) give PBC(h), as in 0A4C; 'proper' and 'surjective' repointed from def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions to def-weil-proper-morphism and def-weil-surjective-morphism; def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property removed from stmt_deps (used only in the proof). 'f proper' is used: PBC(f) is defined only for proper f, the IA equivalence for f and the underived exchange (step 4) need it; it is however implied by h and hf proper (Stacks 01W6, h separated), so the hypotheses 'f, h proper' and 'h, hf proper' are equivalent; hf proper follows from f, h proper by lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition (unit sk-thm-br, used as a tool). Checked the cited nodes: the IA equivalence (lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity, proper f) is used for f, hf (proper by composition) and h; lem-weil-pbc-retract-supplied needs only f surjective but does not name the coefficient category (it must be read in F_r-module sheaves); the underived exchange needs f proper and J torsion; the Grothendieck spectral sequence node has no hypotheses on F; lem-weil-pbc-vanishing-descends-retract is used for h' and the summand b^{-1}I, the additivity of b^{-1} being written in step 7. Hidden arguments made explicit: existence of J (new node lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives, Stacks 01DU), the identification X' = X x_Z Z' (existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting), and the collapse of the spectral sequence (new node lem-weil-pbc-first-quadrant-row-collapse). The imported proof's single paragraph is replaced; its uses lemma-weil-pbc-proper-underived-exchange and lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity, previously only in proof_deps, are now cited by steps.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring which is torsion as an abelian group (every
element has finite additive order; for instance $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$). For a
morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ say that

- $f$ has *torsion base change* over $\Lambda$ if, for every cartesian square
  [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f$ on the right and an arbitrary
  $g:Y'\to Y$ at the bottom, the derived exchange morphism
  [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] $g^{-1}Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$ is an
  isomorphism for every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ whose cohomology sheaves
  are torsion [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf];
- $f$ has *injective acyclicity* over $\Lambda$ if, for every such square and
  every injective sheaf $I$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ which is torsion,
  $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I=0$ for $q>0$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be surjective and $h:Y\to Z$ arbitrary.

1. If $f$ has torsion base change and $hf$ has injective acyclicity over
   $\Lambda$, then $h$ has injective acyclicity over $\Lambda$.
2. If $f$ and $hf$ have torsion base change over $\Lambda$, then so does $h$.

proof.text: Since $\Lambda$ is torsion, every sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules is torsion.

(1) Fix a cartesian square with $h$ on the right and $c:Z'\to Z$ at the bottom;
write $Y'=Y\times_ZZ'$, $X'=X\times_ZZ'$, $b:Y'\to Y$, $a:X'\to X$ and $f'$, $h'$
for the base-changed maps. Let $I$ be an injective sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on
$Y$. Choose a monomorphism $f^{-1}I\hookrightarrow J$ with $J$ injective on $X$.
By [lem-weil-pbc-retract-supplied] ($f$ is surjective) the adjoint map
$s:I\to f_*J$ is a monomorphism, so by injectivity of $I$ it has a retraction
$r$ with $rs=\mathrm{id}_I$. Torsion base change for $f$ implies injective
acyclicity of $f$ and, at the injective sheaf $J$, that the underived exchange
$b^{-1}f_*J\to f'_*a^{-1}J$ is an isomorphism
([lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity]). Thus $a^{-1}J$ is $f'_*$-acyclic,
and the Grothendieck spectral sequence
[lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence] for $X'\xrightarrow{f'}Y'\xrightarrow{h'}Z'$
at $a^{-1}J$ collapses to its row $q=0$ and gives

$$
 R^qh'_*(b^{-1}f_*J)\cong R^qh'_*(f'_*a^{-1}J)\cong R^q(h'f')_*a^{-1}J=0
 \qquad(q>0)
$$

by injective acyclicity of $hf$. The sheaf $b^{-1}I$ is a retract of
$b^{-1}f_*J$ via $b^{-1}s$ and $b^{-1}r$, so
[lem-weil-pbc-vanishing-descends-retract] gives $R^qh'_*b^{-1}I=0$ for $q>0$.

(2) By (1), applied with the injective acyclicity of $hf$ implied by its torsion
base change, $h$ has injective acyclicity. Moreover the underived exchange
morphism $c^{-1}h_*G\to h'_*b^{-1}G$ is an isomorphism for every sheaf $G$ of
$\Lambda$-modules on $Y$: at $G=f_*J$ with $J$ injective this follows from the
vertical pasting of the exchange morphisms of $f$ and $hf$, both isomorphisms at
$J$; a general $G$ is the kernel of a map $f_*J_1\to f_*J_2$ of such sheaves
(the unit $G\to f_*f^{-1}G$ is a monomorphism since $f$ is surjective), and both
sides of the exchange are left exact. Injective acyclicity together with the
underived exchange isomorphism gives torsion base change for $h$
([lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity]). This is Stacks Project, Tag 0A4C.
